title.en: Compute the simple aggregative price index
Compute the simple average of price relatives

say.en: A shopkeeper in Davanagere notes the prices of four items in two years. Can we combine them into one index? There are two simple ways, and they do not always agree. In this lesson: Compute the simple aggregative price index.
Compute the simple average of price relatives.
State the defects of unweighted indices.

body.en: Simple aggregative method: $P_{01} = \frac{\sum P_1}{\sum P_0}\times 100$. Simple average of price relatives: $P_{01} = \frac{1}{n}\sum \frac{P_1}{P_0}\times 100$. In both, every item gets equal importance, so they are called *unweighted* (simple) indices.
body.kn: ಸರಳ ಒಟ್ಟು ಮೊತ್ತ ವಿಧಾನದಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರಸ್ತುತ ಬೆಲೆಗಳ ಮೊತ್ತವನ್ನು ಆಧಾರ ಬೆಲೆಗಳ ಮೊತ್ತದಿಂದ ಭಾಗಿಸಿ 100 ರಿಂದ ಗುಣಿಸುತ್ತೇವೆ. ಬೆಲೆ ಸಾಪೇಕ್ಷಗಳ ಸರಾಸರಿ ವಿಧಾನದಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರತಿ ಸಾಪೇಕ್ಷ ಕಂಡು ಅವುಗಳ ಸರಾಸರಿ ತೆಗೆಯುತ್ತೇವೆ.

title.en: Why simple indices are not enough

body.en: In the simple aggregative method, items with high prices dominate, and changing the unit (price per kg instead of per quintal) changes the answer. Both simple methods give equal importance to salt and to rice, although a family spends far more on rice. Weighted *indices* correct this.
body.kn: ಸರಳ ಸೂಚ್ಯಂಕಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಎರಡು ದೋಷಗಳಿವೆ: ದುಬಾರಿ ವಸ್ತುಗಳು ಒಟ್ಟು ಮೊತ್ತ ಸೂಚ್ಯಂಕದಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರಾಬಲ್ಯ ಹೊಂದುತ್ತವೆ, ಮತ್ತು ಎಲ್ಲ ವಸ್ತುಗಳಿಗೆ ಸಮಾನ ಪ್ರಾಮುಖ್ಯ ನೀಡಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ತೂಕದ ಸೂಚ್ಯಂಕಗಳು ಇದನ್ನು ಸರಿಪಡಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

points.en: Units of measurement affect the *aggregative* index

problem.en: Base prices of rice, wheat and sugar are ₹10, ₹20, ₹30; current prices are ₹15, ₹25, ₹40. Find both simple indices.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. Base prices of rice, wheat and sugar are ₹10, ₹20, ₹30; current prices are ₹15, ₹25, ₹40. Find both simple indices.

say.en: Let us work this out together. Base prices of rice, wheat and sugar are 10, rupees 20, rupees 30 rupees; current prices are 15, rupees 25, rupees 40 rupees. Find both simple indices.
ΣP0 equals 60, ΣP1 equals 80. Aggregative index equals 80 divided by 60 times 100 equals 133.33.
Relatives: 15 over 10 times 100 equals 150; 25 over 20 times 100 equals 125; 40 over 30 times 100 equals 133.33.
Average of relatives equals 150 plus 125 plus 133.33 divided by 3 equals 408.33 divided by 3 equals 136.11.
So the answer is Aggregative 133.33; average of relatives 136.11.

body.en: Aggregative: Add first, then divide. Relatives: Divide first, then average. The order of the two steps is the whole difference.
